name: japanlaw
description: Japanese law, answered from the statute itself: the Japanese as published, the Ministry of Justice's English where there is one and marked machine translation where there is not, every provision quoted with its link. Read-only tools from japanlaw.org's MCP server, and a skill that teaches how a Japanese provision is cited and which English may be quoted.

interface.longDescription:
Japanese law, answered from the statute itself: the Japanese as published, the Ministry of Justice's English where there is one and marked machine translation where there is not, every provision quoted with its link. Read-only tools from japanlaw.org's MCP server, and a skill that teaches how a Japanese provision is cited and which English may be quoted.

For anyone who has to deal with a Japanese law: a worker, an employer, someone new to Japan, a lawyer abroad. Ask what an article says, what a word in a law means, or what an amendment changed, and the answer quotes the provision, links its page on japanlaw.org, and says whose English it is.

No account, no key and nothing to configure. What you ask is not recorded. It is information about the law, not legal advice.
capabilities: Read a provision or a law
Look up the words a law defines
See what changes across the laws
defaultPrompt: Under Japanese law, how many hours of overtime can my employer ask of me in a month? Quote the article.
What does Article 36 of the Labor Standards Act say? Show the Japanese and say whose English it is.
I'm renting an apartment in Tokyo. When can the landlord refuse to renew the lease?

positive.description: Quote a provision by its article number, with whose English it is
positive.prompt: What does Article 36 of Japan's Labor Standards Act say? Quote the Japanese and say whose English it is.
positive.expected_behavior: Quotes 第三十六条 in Japanese with the Ministry of Justice's English, says the English is the Ministry's translation, and links https://japanlaw.org/en/labor-standards-act/art-36.

positive.description: Answer a reader's question from the statute
positive.prompt: Can my employer in Japan refuse the days I asked for as paid leave?
positive.expected_behavior: Explains Article 39(5) of the Labor Standards Act: leave is granted at the time the worker asks, and the employer may move it only where that would interfere with the normal operation of the business. Quotes the paragraph and links it.

positive.description: Look up a word the law defines
positive.prompt: In the Labor Standards Act, what does 労働者 (worker) mean? Quote the law's definition.
positive.expected_behavior: Quotes the definition in Article 9 — a person employed at a business or office and paid wages, whatever the kind of job — and links Article 9.

positive.description: List what changes across the laws on a day
positive.prompt: Which Japanese laws change on 1 April 2027?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the laws held that change on 1 April 2027 with each amending Act — the Labor Standards Act by Act No. 60 of 2026 among them — and links each change.

positive.description: Find the provisions that cite a provision
positive.prompt: Which provisions cite Article 36, paragraph (1) of the Labor Standards Act?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists provisions that cite it, such as Articles 32-3-2 and 32-4-2 of the same Act, each with its link, and says how many there are in all.

negative.description: A provision that does not exist: the tool says so, and nothing is invented
negative.prompt: Show me Article 999 of the Labor Standards Act.

negative.description: A law japanlaw.org does not hold: say it is not held rather than quote it from memory
negative.prompt: What does the Tokyo Metropolitan Ordinance on noise say?

negative.description: An action the read-only tools cannot take: say they only read the law
negative.prompt: File my final income tax return for me.

review.commerce_description: japanlaw.org sells nothing and processes no payments; every tool only reads the law.
